classification.difficultyReason: Choose the shared diagonal as an intermediate length, obtain it by the sine rule in one triangle and use it with the cosine rule in the other.

content.prompt:
A pipeline needs to be constructed from points $A$ to $B$ across a marshland. The engineers cannot measure length $AB$ directly, so they mark out two additional points $D$ and $C$. Their measurements are summarised on the diagram below.

Find the length of the proposed pipe, correct to the nearest metre.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 diagram in the right column
spec.description: Triangles ABD and ACD share AD. AB crosses an irregular marsh region; decorative reeds are omitted. Light green identifies the inaccessible terrain.
spec.mathematics: BD = 165 m; AC = 125 m; angle BDA = 70 degrees; angle DAC = 25 degrees; angle ACD = 95 degrees. Coordinates are derived from these givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and vertex labels are visible; AD and AB remain unlabelled.

answer.short:
$178\,\mathrm{m}$.

Find $AD$ using the sine rule, then find $AB$ using the cosine rule.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ACD$,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle ADC &= 180^\circ-25^\circ-95^\circ\\
\angle ADC &= 60^\circ.
\end{align*}$$
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{AD}{\sin95^\circ} &= \frac{125}{\sin60^\circ}\\
AD &= \frac{125\sin95^\circ}{\sin60^\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
By the cosine rule in $\triangle ABD$,
$$\begin{align*}
AB^2 &= AD^2+165^2-2(AD)(165)\cos70^\circ\\
AB &= \sqrt{\left(\frac{125\sin95^\circ}{\sin60^\circ}\right)^2+165^2-330\left(\frac{125\sin95^\circ}{\sin60^\circ}\right)\cos70^\circ}\\
AB &\approx 178\,\mathrm{m}.
\end{align*}$$
The proposed pipe is approximately $178\,\mathrm{m}$ long, to the nearest metre.
